name: sgr_press_button1
why: low two bits select the button; 0 means button1

name: sgr_press_button2
why: low two bits select the button; 1 means button2

name: sgr_press_button3
why: low two bits select the button; 2 means button3

name: sgr_release_button1
why: a final lowercase m is a release regardless of the button bits

name: sgr_release_no_button
why: button bits 3 names no button, but a release must still end a drag and MouseFlags has no button-agnostic release, so button 1 is chosen deliberately here (see README, stated assumptions)

name: sgr_press_shift
why: bit 2 shift, bit 3 alt, bit 4 ctrl; 4 sets shift

name: sgr_press_alt
why: bit 2 shift, bit 3 alt, bit 4 ctrl; 8 sets alt

name: sgr_press_ctrl
why: bit 2 shift, bit 3 alt, bit 4 ctrl; 16 sets ctrl

name: sgr_press_shift_ctrl
why: bit 2 shift, bit 3 alt, bit 4 ctrl; 20 sets shift_ctrl

name: sgr_press_all_three
why: bit 2 shift, bit 3 alt, bit 4 ctrl; 28 sets all_three

name: sgr_motion_button1_held
why: bit 5 is motion; with a button in the low bits it is a drag

name: sgr_motion_no_button
why: bit 5 set and button bits 3: motion with nothing held

name: sgr_wheel_up
why: bit 6 is the wheel; low bits then select the direction, 64 is up

name: sgr_wheel_down
why: bit 6 is the wheel; low bits then select the direction, 65 is down

name: sgr_wheel_left
why: bit 6 is the wheel; low bits then select the direction, 66 is left

name: sgr_wheel_right
why: bit 6 is the wheel; low bits then select the direction, 67 is right

name: sgr_wheel_up_ctrl
why: the wheel carries modifiers in the same bits as a button does

name: sgr_origin
why: the wire is 1-based, so the smallest legal coordinate is 1;1

name: sgr_past_x10_limit
why: SGR has no 223 ceiling; a coordinate X10 cannot express must still decode

name: x10_press_button1
why: every byte carries value+32, so button 0 at 9;5 is 0x20 0x29 0x25

name: x10_press_button3
why: the same low two bits as SGR select the button

name: x10_release
why: X10 cannot say which button a release was for, so button 1 is chosen, the same deliberate choice as the SGR release

name: x10_press_shift
why: modifiers sit in the same bits as SGR, not in the button number

name: x10_wheel_up
why: bit 6 is the wheel here too

name: paste_plain
why: ESC[200~ opens and ESC[201~ closes; what lies between is text, not keys

name: paste_containing_escape
why: inside a paste an escape is DATA; decoding it as a key is the classic bug

name: paste_empty
why: an open immediately followed by a close is a paste of nothing

name: key_uparrow
why: CSI A is cursor up

name: key_downarrow
why: CSI B is cursor down

name: key_rightarrow
why: CSI C is cursor right

name: key_leftarrow
why: CSI D is cursor left

name: key_home
why: CSI H is home

name: key_end
why: CSI F is end

name: key_shift_tab
why: CSI Z is back-tab, which is shift+tab

name: sgr_truncated
why: a report cut off mid-parameter cannot be decoded; it must not be guessed at

name: sgr_missing_final
why: no M or m means no terminator, so the sequence is incomplete

name: sgr_press_no_button
why: button bits 3 names no button, and a press of no button holds nothing down: no button flag, and the position is all there is left to report (see README, stated assumptions)
